question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to register arbitrary stdio MCP commands in the global OpenClaw MCP configuration, or must every command and shared declaration pass an explicit host-controlled broker and authorization boundary?
rationale: The correct boundary determines whether this feature remains a convenience layer over trusted local configuration or becomes a new role-to-host code-execution capability; that policy cannot be safely inferred from the current implementation.

options.title: Require brokered, scoped MCP ownership
options.body: Accept only host-approved command paths and explicit shared-resource grants, with per-Claw namespacing or equivalent ownership isolation.

options.title: Treat Claws as fully trusted local configuration
options.body: Permit global command registration and exact sharing, while documenting that every Claw manifest has the same local execution authority as the host.

recommendation.title: Require brokered, scoped MCP ownership
recommendation.body: Accept only host-approved command paths and explicit shared-resource grants, with per-Claw namespacing or equivalent ownership isolation.
